title: Prototype pollution, duplicate-key smuggling and JSON denial-of-service defense
attackSurface: Attacker-supplied JSON parsed at an API trust boundary

hostile.title: Dunder proto pollution
hostile.why: Direct prototype key used by classic JavaScript merge attacks

hostile.title: Prototype property pollution
hostile.why: Prototype-shaped keys are dangerous when merged into object graphs

hostile.title: Exact duplicate key
hostile.why: Duplicate-key parser differentials can smuggle a second security decision

hostile.title: Unicode duplicate key
hostile.why: Escaped and literal spellings decode to the same object key

hostile.title: Deep nesting denial of service
hostile.why: Deep recursion or parser stack use is a classic JSON denial-of-service primitive

hostile.title: Unsafe integer precision
hostile.why: Values beyond the exact safe-integer range create identity and authorization confusion

hostile.title: Oversized string denial of service
hostile.why: Bounded APIs must reject payloads beyond their configured byte budget

benign.title: Unicode content
benign.why: Valid UTF-16 JSON text with non-ASCII content

benign.title: Moderate nested object
benign.why: Nested configuration data inside the strict depth budget

benign.title: Keys near prototype words
benign.why: Strings containing dangerous words are not themselves prototype keys

benign.title: Escaped unicode distinct keys
benign.why: Unicode escape spelling is valid when it does not duplicate another key

benign.title: Medium string within budget
benign.why: Legitimate text under the configured payload cap
